'''''Star Wars: Galactic Atlas''''' is a reference book that was published by [[Egmont]] UK Ltd on [[November 3]], [[2016]]. An atlas with full-color illustrations by [[Tim McDonagh]], it covers the first seven ''[[Star Wars]]'' films, as well as ''[[Star Wars Rebels]]'', ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'', novels, and comics. The American edition was published by [[Disney–Lucasfilm Press]] on [[December 20]], [[2016]]. It is titled '''''Star Wars Galactic Maps: An Illustrated Atlas of the Star Wars Universe''''' and includes a spread relating to the then-upcoming film ''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]''.

While working on the video game ''[[Star Wars Battlefront II]]'', the development team notably consulted the ''Galactic Atlas''.<ref name="BTS">{{EASWYouTube|pryBP4K-_34|Star Wars Battlefront II: Behind The Story}}</ref> An [[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas: Updated Edition|updated edition]] of ''Galactic Atlas'' was released on [[November 6]], [[2025]].<ref name="2025Amazon">{{WebCite|url=https://www.bonnierbooks.co.uk/books/studio-press/star-wars-galactic-atlas/|text=Star Wars Galactic Atlas|work=[[Wikipedia:Bonnier Group|Bonnier Books]]|archivedate=20251109224027}}</ref>

==Publisher's summary==
''Explore the worlds and stories of a galaxy far, far away with this lavishly illustrated Galactic Atlas! Follow the beasts, battles, heroes and villains of the Star Wars saga all the way from the deserts of Tatooine to the ice plains of Hoth.''

*''Stunning full-colour illustrations by Tim McDonagh''
*''Covers all seven films, as well as Star Wars Rebels, The Clone Wars, novels and comics''
*''A perfect gift for fans of all ages!''

==Continuity==
===Continuity errors===
As depicted in [[Star Wars: Episode VII The Force Awakens|''Star Wars'': Episode VII ''The Force Awakens'']], the firing of the [[Starkiller Base]] [[superlaser]] destroyed the five [[planet]]s of the [[Hosnian system]];<ref name="Episode VII">{{Film|VII}}</ref> however, the ''Galactic Atlas''{{'s}} entry for Starkiller Base instead states that the weapon's firing destroyed "five [[star system]]s".<ref name="SWGA">[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]</ref>

On page 18, within the [[Dathomir]] spread, at the top information box, the [[Quelii sector]] is misspelled as the "Qelii sector".<ref name="SWGA" />

===The Zakuul empire conundrum===
{{Quote|to answer your question, the Atlas is supposed to be canon, 'Zakuul' isn't.|Emil Fortune|<ref name="Twitter 2">{{Twitter|iucounu|status/811974480813846528|[[Emil Fortune]]|quote=to answer your question, the Atlas is supposed to be canon, 'Zakuul' isn't.|archiveurl=https://archive.is/lftem}}</ref>}}
The [[December]] [[2016]] Polish edition of ''Star Wars: Galactic Atlas'' includes an entry for the [[Eternal Empire|Empire]] of [[Zakuul]], placing it in the far west of [[the galaxy]] and in the [[Unknown Regions]]. The [[Zakuulan]] empire is a [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] entity that was first mentioned in [[2015]] on [http://swtor.com swtor.com] for the expansion [[Star Wars: The Old Republic: Knights of the Fallen Empire|''Knights of the Fallen Empire'']] of the [[BioWare]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''.<ref name="TORweb">{{TORweb|url=fallen-empire|text=Knights of the Fallen Empire}}</ref> The author of ''Galactic Atlas'', [[Emil Fortune]], stated that he did not know why or how Zakuul crept into the Polish translation of the reference book.<ref name="Twitter">{{Twitter|iucounu|status/811973938108657665|[[Emil Fortune]]|quote=I wrote the Atlas; Zakuul seems to have crept into the Polish translation only. I am not sure why or how as yet.|archivedate=20210313095450}}</ref> Nonetheless, he stated that the world was not supposed to be canonical.<ref name="Twitter 2" /> [[Zakuul system|A system bearing the same name]] was introduced into canon by the [[Star Systems of the Galaxy]] appendix, with the system having a similar placement in the far west of the galaxy.<ref name="GalaxyMapAppendix">{{GalaxyMapAppendix}}</ref>
